chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The pregnant divorced woman is provided for until she gives birth to her child, and she is more deserving of her son if she breastfeeds him, for the amount that another woman would accept.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child, and upon the heir is similar to that.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman from us would raise her hand to her husband when he wanted to have intercourse with her, so she would say,

And as for His words 'and upon the heir is similar to that', then He forbade that the child be harmed, or his mother be harmed regarding his breastfeeding. And it is not for her to take (recompense) for his breastfeeding for more than two complete years. And if they both intend weaning before that by mutual consent, it is good. And weaning is the cessation of breastfeeding.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِوَلَدِهَا: More deserving of her child (custody priority)
key_terms.تَضَعَ حَمْلَهَا: She gives birth to her child
key_terms.لا تُضَارَّ: Neither shall be made to suffer harm

ai.seo_question: What are the financial and custody rights of a pregnant divorced woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the financial maintenance (nafaqah) and custody rights of a pregnant divorced woman, emphasizing the Quranic principle of 'no harm' (la tudarr) to prevent either party from exploiting the other. It clarifies that while the mother has priority in breastfeeding, the compensation is limited to two complete years, with early weaning permissible by mutual consent, reflecting the Shia scholarly focus on balancing maternal rights with equitable distribution of burdens.
